summary: An L-4 cab built about 1933 on a Bob Marshall Wilderness summit and abandoned in the mid-1950s; a 1937 season is documented in a Montana newspaper.

facts.status_note: The cab was abandoned in the mid-1950s and is gone. No source describes what remains on the summit.

events.note: Seasonal lookout occupied through the 1937 summer, per a 1937 newspaper article
Source says abandoned in the mid-1950s; 1955 is an approximate year

evidence.quote: Located in the Bob Marshall Wilderness

evidence.supports: camp on the summit in the 1920s
evidence.quote: first home to a camp established in the 1920's
This L-4 cab was constructed about 1933

evidence.supports: 1937 season, Carter County high school student
evidence.quote: to resume his studies in the Carter county high school
The lookout which was in the Flathead forest required a 70-mile journey into the forest by airplane from Kalispell.

evidence.supports: 10-mile pack-train ride from Big Prairie ranger station
evidence.quote: Frank had a further trip of 10 miles by pack train to reach his cabin

evidence.supports: Big Prairie ranger station as the starting point

evidence.quote: Here in a cabin 14x14 he watched for fires

evidence.supports: water carried up from a stream 2 1/4 miles down
evidence.quote: For water, he went 2 1/4 miles down the mountain
there secured it from a stream

evidence.supports: water carried up to the cabin in a sack
evidence.quote: This he carried in a canvas sack on his back, 40 pounds in weight, back to his mountain home.
The summer was an unusually good one for the forest service for there were very few fires.
Sentinel Mountain Lewis & Clark 47.38500 -113.05253 Ground Gone

sources.title: Sentinel Mountain, Forest Lookouts, western US

notes_for_editor: Only firelookout.com gives the cab's construction date and abandonment; the 1937 article confirms occupancy only. 'Mid-1950s' is approximate, so the abandonment event is dated 1955 with that caveat. Two web searches found nothing else on this lookout. Search snippets pointed to Mount Sentinel above Missoula, a different lookout, which is not used. Brief's agency, county and coordinates match the FFLA list; no location conflict. Access: no source describes a route or current status of the site; the story says only that it is in the wilderness.
